success_criteria.notes: Success if the assistant schedules the Zoo Field Trip outdoor event at Minneapolis Zoo via create_meeting for 180 minutes.

task.objective: Schedule an outdoor field trip to the zoo

injected_behaviors.instructions: The user wants to schedule a field trip for their students and prefers Saturday but wants to check the weather first.

persona.name: Maria Gonzalez
persona.bio: Maria Gonzalez teaches English to adult immigrants in Miami, helping them improve language skills for work and daily life. She plans interactive lessons, assigns practical homework, and connects students with community resources. Many of her students are juggling jobs and families while learning English.
sample_messages: Class on Thursday - can you print 20 copies of the job interview worksheet?
Looking for conversational English practice resources, preferably free or low-cost for students
Workshop on teaching pronunciation next month - can you check if there's professional development funding available?

messages.output_raw: I want to set up a field trip to the zoo for my class on a Saturday. Can you help me schedule it and also check what the weather will be like?

steps.output_raw:
<think>
User wants outdoor event on a Saturday, needs scheduling plus weather. Need date, location (which zoo/city), and maybe time window; also if they want me to actually check calendar availability via tools or just suggest. Weather tool exists; use check_weather_forecast and maybe suggest_alternative_dates if bad. First, I must clarify missing info (which Saturday/date, which zoo/city, approximate time) before calling any tools. Keep it concise. </think>
<plan>
1. Ask clarifying questions about the specific Saturday/date, zoo/location, and approximate time window.
2. Once I have the date and location, call the weather forecast tool for that date and location.
3. If weather looks poor, optionally suggest better alternative dates using the alternative-dates tool.
4. Help the user outline/schedule the field trip timing and logistics based on their answers.
</plan>
